A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SonicMaster research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original restoration benchmarks, model and conditioning ablations, historical-piano evaluations, and two listening studies in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices A.8–A.9, including objective scores and listener preferences.

M1.justification: The VAE/FLAN-T5 conditioning, MM-DiT/DiT architecture, rectified-flow objective, Euler update, and overlapping-segment processing are retained. v4 supplies additional formal and implementation descriptions without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use the same Jamendo-derived corpus, ten genre groups, nineteen degradations, snippet and full-song evaluations, RemFX dynamics/reverb tests, and historical piano recordings. Proposed cultural and real-world dataset expansions in v4 are future work.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Text2FX cosine/directional variants, Mel2Mel + DiffWave, WPE/HPSS, the five removal-model comparators, and LTAS-EQ, BEHM-GAN, BABE, and BABE-2. Naming refinements and relocated ablations do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The training budget, 7,000-clip test set and 1,000 clean references, metrics, solver configurations, and 12- and 20-participant listening-study designs match. The additional study instructions in v4 document the existing evaluation rather than establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Solver, architecture-size, audio-conditioning, missing-text, and shuffled-prompt ablations are retained, with details consolidated in v4 Appendix A.9. The same restoration spectrograms and generalization analyses remain; no new controlled robustness or sensitivity analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both retain the listening-study 95% confidence intervals, paired t-tests and significance thresholds, and Table 4's mean-plus/minus reporting. v4 introduces no additional seed information, repeated-run reporting, or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched quantitative results, plotted findings, and spectrogram examples are unchanged, including text-ablation rows moved into Tables 8–10. Appendix A.10 newly reports occasional volume inconsistency over a track, adding a limited qualitative failure finding without new measurements.

T1.justification: The interpolation, loss, and metric definitions are retained. However, new Equation (9) states dx/dt = f_theta, conflicting with the retained v = -dx/dt convention and positive Euler update when stepping toward t = 0. This introduces a local inconsistency in the formal inference description; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v4 explicitly narrows 'mastering' to single-song perceptual enhancement, excluding album-level cohesion and the full professional mastering workflow. The central claims of unified, text-controlled restoration of nineteen degradations and creation of the paired corpus remain.

C2.justification: v3 mainly discusses latent-space artifacts and long-form/reverb difficulties. v4 substantially expands applicability boundaries through its introduction, discussion, and new Appendix A.10: Western-cultural bias, synthetic-data coverage, specialized language ambiguity, restricted mastering scope, and temporal consistency. It also adds an impact discussion concerning production work and human expertise.

D1.justification: v4 identifies GPT-4o for contrast prompts, specifies direct conditioned inference without guidance interpolation, and documents the Psytoolkit platform, participant briefing, questions, and interface. It removes v3's explicit commitment to release training, inference, evaluation code, and data upon acceptance, while retaining the model link and corpus-release claim; actual resource withdrawal is not established.

R1.justification: v4 adds production-language context through Moffat, Pras, and Wilmering, plus two Stoet references for Psytoolkit. It removes the InstructMe and Martinez-Ramirez out-of-domain mixing references. These are limited changes in positioning; numerous other reference edits update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: related work and experimental descriptions are condensed, architecture explanations are expanded into named components, and detailed ablation and comparative-listening discussions move to the appendix. New limitations and impact sections further change the document structure.

P2.justification: The main text switches from one column to two. The separate dataset and architecture diagrams are replaced by a combined redraw, a listening-interface screenshot is added, and the comparative preference chart and text-ablation rows move to the appendix. Tables and spectrogram displays are extensively resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves transparency and interpretation by defining the limits of mastering, explaining data and language limitations, and documenting the listening study more concretely. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. These benefits outweigh the localized new Equation (9) sign inconsistency and loss of the explicit release commitment, but those drawbacks limit the overall improvement.
